summary.headline: Emmvee FY26 revenue rose 116% to INR 5,049 crore and PAT 193% to INR 1,082 crore, with 9.4 GW order book and 6 GW expansion underway.
summary.overview: FY26 was the first year as a listed company (IPO Nov 2025, INR 2,900 crore raised), with revenue of INR 5,049 crore, EBITDA of INR 1,734 crore (34% margin) and PAT of INR 1,082 crore (21% margin). Module capacity reached 10.3 GW after two 2.5 GW lines were commissioned (May and Dec 2025), and cell utilisation rose to 69.9% for the year and 79% in Q4. Working capital absorbed cash as inventory built up, while the 6 GW integrated cell and module project at Devanahalli is progressing with IREDA's INR 3,306 crore loan sanctioned. Management stated that FY27 will be a year of execution.

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 10.3 GW at March 31, 2026, 100% TOPCon; module utilisation 43% for FY26, affected by Units 5 and 6 running only part-year. Q4 module production about 953 MW per management in Q&A, and G12R modules now in production.

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 2.94 GW; utilisation 69.9% in FY26 (43.3% in FY25), 79% in Q4 and about 85% in March 2026. Management expects a transition from M10 to G12R cells by end of the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: 6 GW integrated cell and module facility at Devanahalli: module line commissioning expected by end of calendar 2026, cell line by end of FY27.
Post-expansion installed capacity targeted at 16.3 GW modules and 8.9 GW cells by end of FY27.
Ingot and wafer facility of about 9 GW in phases: Phase 1 5 GW, Phase 2 4 GW a year later; first facility planned in FY29. Capex guided at INR 600-700 crore per GW.
Next-quarter DCR mix guided at 30-35% of module sales; by around the beginning of FY28 management expects nearly all sold capacity to be DCR.
Current EBITDA spreads on new orders said to be similar to FY26 levels.
IREDA term loan of INR 3,306 crore at 7.95%; about 75-80% expected to be drawn by March 2027, with 15-20% retention spilling into FY28.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex in cash flow about INR 650 crore; gross block rise of about INR 1,000 crore (adjusted for grant) mainly for Units 5 and 6 modules. Land acquisition of about INR 311 crore for the expansion was expensed this year per the Q&A.
Module line commissioning: 2.5 GW in May 2025 and 2.5 GW in Dec 2025 at Sulibele, Bengaluru.
Land at Devanahalli fully paid and in possession; construction started and module line order finalised.
Management cited that module lines typically reach 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, which is why module capacity is sized above cell capacity.
Cell capacity at 2.94 GW already built for G12 and line can switch from M10 to G12R through a kit change.
demand_pricing: DCR module price about INR 21-22/W; non-DCR module about INR 14-15/W. Management says DCR pricing is resilient and has not seen upward pressure despite limited domestic cell capacity.
Customer mix cited: IPPs about 40%, C&I about 30% (from prior analyst framing; not contradicted). Average top-10 customer order size rose to 221 MW from 121 MW.

Demand drivers cited: PM-KUSUM (KUSUM-C) and PM Surya Ghar for DCR; ALMM List-2 for cells expected to phase in, with utility projects bid after August 2025 covered; ALMM for IPP demand expected around FY28 or late 2027.
Exports: zero in FY26 and no export orders in the book; management treats exports as upside.
A customer advance of about INR 320 crore received in FY25 was adjusted this year, lowering the customer advance balance. A 4.5 GW cell order has been advanced in full and supply has started.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory build up, and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the build reflects the ramp-up in Q4 (revenue about INR 1,700 crore, versus about INR 1,000 crore in Q1); CFO said FY26 finished-goods change was INR 636 crore and inventory should be held near current levels, with some reduction possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the production-to-revenue gap large (revenue +67% QoQ vs production +30%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales differ from production, realisations move with raw-material prices, and EBITDA per watt is the better measure; it does not disclose sales MW.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 6 GW cell plan 9 GW versus module 7 GW in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said modules run at 65-70% utilisation versus 90-95% for cells, so module capacity is sized higher to match cell output; module is made to order, cell is batch made-to-stock.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines and quantum for the wafer/ingot plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Ingot-wafer of about 9 GW in phases, first facility in FY29, capex about INR 600-700 crore per GW.

qa_highlights.question: IREDA loan rate and drawdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Rate 7.95%; nothing drawn yet, first drawdown expected within about a month; 75-80% expected drawn by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of a possible ALMM delay to July?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a one-to-two-month shift would not change plans; it sees no change in DCR/non-DCR mix from a few-month delay.

risks_watch: Working capital: inventory and receivables rose; operating cash after working-capital change fell to about INR 200 crore from about INR 625 crore, per analyst calculation.
Module utilisation at 43% for FY26; Q4 module output and the ramp of Units 5 and 6 need to be tracked.
Capex of about INR 4,500-4,800 crore for the 6 GW project plus INR 600-700 crore per GW for ingot-wafer; funding mix (debt/equity) not finalised.
ALMM timing: developers have petitioned for an earlier July deadline; utility bids after August 2025 are covered.
Cell transition from M10 to G12R, targeted by end of the current quarter; ramp risk on cell utilisation.
April cell production on the DCR portal looked lower; management said the portal updates monthly and that production continues normally.
Inter-company eliminations rose sharply in Q4 between the parent and the Emmvee Energy subsidiary; the accounting is not fully detailed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, execution and balance sheet, but guarded on pricing and cash flow. Management was direct on capacity and loan terms, but deflected on exact DCR mix (giving a 30-35% range) and on sales volumes, which it does not disclose.
key_quotes: FY26 was a milestone year; FY27 will be the year of execution.
Growth must, therefore, be measured against returns, leverage, execution timelines and customer visibility.
So, we don't have any Mono PERC capacity; all our capacity is TOPCon and latest.
exports are treated as an upside for us rather than the core part of our business in the current scenarios.
